set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. Housing Trust Placer is a private nonprofit that publishes no NOFA or loan guidelines and its website says nothing on prevailing wage. Coverage follows the public sources it assembles: County funds can make a project public works under Labor Code 1720(b), subject to 1720(c)(3) de minimis (under $600,000 and under 2% of project cost) and 1720(c)(5)(E) below-market loans with 40% of units at 80% AMI or below for 20 years; its down payment programs fall under the 1720(c)(5)(C) exemption for down payment assistance. Any HOME, CDBG or state money layered in carries that program's own rule.

reason: The trust's site and County materials state no prevailing wage rule, and Labor Code 1720 coverage depends on each project's public sources and the 1720(c) exemptions.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. The September 16, 2026 Council packet (Sierra Vista deferral, Resolution 26-336) does not address prevailing wage. A fee deferral at the City's pooled interest rate may be a reduced fee or below-market interest rate under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), but 1720(b)(4) alone does not decide coverage; the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test (under $600,000 and under 2% of project cost) and the 1720(c)(5)(E) below-market loan exemption (40% of units at 80% AMI or below for 20 years) may apply, and Roseville's separate CDBG loan to the same sponsor brings its own federal rule.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. The September 9, 2025 AHIP staff report (Ordinance 1159 fee reduction, SB 937 deferral) does not address prevailing wage. A 40% impact fee reduction is a reduced or waived fee under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), but coverage depends on the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test (under $600,000 and under 2% of project cost); projects using only Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund money plus private funds are exempt under 1720(c)(4), but adding the fee reduction may take a project outside that exemption, and 1720(c)(5)(E) may apply to below-market loans at 40% of units at 80% AMI or below.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. The adopted 2021 Housing Element (Programs A and I) does not address prevailing wage. Negotiated fee reductions or land write-downs are reduced fees or below-market land under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) and (b)(3), with coverage depending on the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test and 1720(c)(5) exemptions. If the City secures state CDBG or HOME for a project, those programs carry their own federal rules (Davis-Bacon for CDBG at 8+ units, HOME 24 CFR 92.354 at 12+ HOME units), but those are separate awards.
